title: UPPER PUSH AND POSTURE
subtitle: SEATED FIRST, THEN STANDING AT THE WALL AND CHAIR. NO FLOOR TODAY. KIND HIPS.

script.welcome: Good morning Pam. I'm Stratton. Tuesday is upper body and posture, about eleven minutes. We start seated with light arms work, then stand for wall push ups, a kind hip stretch, and a little balance. No floor today. Light weights or empty hands are both perfect, and a smaller range is fine on sore-joint days. Well done for showing up.
script.start: Whenever you're ready. Sit tall near the front of a sturdy chair, feet flat, shoulders soft, easy breath.
script.nextExercise: Next one. Settle in. No rush.
script.lastSet: Last one of these. Keep it comfortable.
script.complete: That's us, Pam. Upper body and posture done, shoulders back and a proper little break from the desk. Have a sip of water. Well done.
script.pause: Paused. Take all the time you need.
script.resume: Back with you. Easy as we go.

exercises.name: SEATED ROW (SQUEEZE)
exercises.cue: Sit tall near the front of the chair, feet flat. Reach both arms forward at chest height, empty hands or light weights. Draw the elbows back close to the ribs and gently squeeze the shoulder blades together, chest proud, then reach forward again slowly. Eight easy reps. Shoulders stay down away from the ears. Empty hands are perfectly fine. Keep the hips relaxed and the torso tall. Stop if you feel sharp groin pain, spreading pain, numbness, tingling, or weakness.
exercises.speakStart: Seated row to wake up the posture. Two rounds of eight. Reach forward, draw the elbows back, gentle squeeze between the shoulder blades. Empty hands are fine.
exercises.speakRest: Twenty seconds. Arms down. Easy breath.

exercises.name: SEATED OVERHEAD PRESS (LIGHT)
exercises.cue: Still seated tall, feet flat. Hands at shoulder height, palms forward, empty or with light weights. Press up slowly as far as is comfortable, then lower with control. Full overhead is not required — halfway is fine on sore-shoulder or sore-joint days. Ribs stay down, no arching the back. Six easy reps. Stop if you feel sharp groin pain, spreading pain, numbness, tingling, or weakness.
exercises.speakStart: Seated overhead press, nice and light. Two rounds of six. Press up slowly, only as high as is comfortable, then lower with control. Halfway is fine.
exercises.speakRest: Twenty seconds. Hands down. Roll the shoulders gently.

exercises.name: SEATED FIGURE FOUR (LIGHT)
exercises.cue: Still seated tall, feet flat. Cross the left ankle lightly over the right knee into a gentle figure-four. Do not push the knee down. Stay upright or add the tiniest hinge forward for a mild stretch in the outer hip. Breathe slowly for about twenty seconds, then try the other side if it feels kind. If the front of the left hip pinches, skip this one entirely. Stop if you feel sharp groin pain, spreading pain, numbness, tingling, or weakness.
exercises.speakStart: Seated figure four, nice and light. About twenty seconds each side. Ankle lightly over the other knee, sit tall, no forcing. Skip it if the front of the hip pinches.
exercises.speakRest: Fifteen seconds. Uncross gently. Then we stand up for the rest.
exercises.speakDone: Figure four done. Kind work for the hips. Up on your feet now, take your time.

exercises.name: WALL PUSH-UPS
exercises.cue: Stand facing the wall, about an arm's length away, feet hip-width. Hands flat on the wall at shoulder height, a little wider than the shoulders. Bend the elbows to bring the chest toward the wall, then press back slowly. Body stays in one long line, no sagging at the hips. Stand closer to the wall to make it easier. Six easy reps. On a sore-joint day, make the bend small. Stop if you feel sharp groin pain, spreading pain, numbness, tingling, or weakness.
exercises.speakStart: Wall push ups, our main push move. Two rounds of six. Hands on the wall, lean in slowly, press back. Step closer to make it easier.
exercises.speakRest: Twenty five seconds. Step back from the wall. Shake out the arms.
exercises.speakDone: Wall push ups done. Well pushed, Pam.

exercises.name: STANDING HIP FLEXOR
exercises.cue: Stand beside the chair with the right hand lightly on the chair back. Step the left foot back about half a step — not a deep lunge — both feet pointing forward, knees soft. Gently tuck the pelvis under (belt buckle toward the ribs) until you feel a mild stretch at the front of the left hip. A tiny lean is enough. Breathe slowly for about twenty seconds. Small and kind, never aggressive. A lovely undo for all the sitting. Stop if you feel sharp groin pain, spreading pain, numbness, tingling, or weakness.
exercises.speakStart: Standing hip flexor, left leg back. Two holds of about twenty seconds. Small step back, pelvis tucked, tiny lean. Kind and small.
exercises.speakRest: Fifteen seconds. Feet together. Easy breath.

exercises.name: CHAIR BALANCE
exercises.cue: Stand behind or beside the sturdy chair with one or both hands on the chair back. Stand tall, shoulders back from the rowing. Shift your weight onto one foot and lift the other heel, or the whole foot just an inch, for about fifteen seconds. Then switch sides. Eyes on a fixed point ahead, breathe. Hold the chair as firmly as you need. If the left hip grumbles when standing on it, keep the toes of the other foot lightly touching the floor. Stop if anything feels sharp or wobbly in a worrying way.
exercises.speakStart: Chair balance to finish. About fifteen seconds each side. Hands on the chair, stand tall, lift one foot a little, eyes ahead. Hold on as much as you like.
exercises.speakRest: Ten seconds. Both feet down. Easy breath.
exercises.speakDone: Balance done. That's the session, Pam. Tall posture and strong arms. Have a grand Tuesday.
